name: Passive emerging market currency basket

origin.source_title: Emerging Market Currency Excess Returns (NBER WP 14528, 2008; AEJ: Macroeconomics 3(4), 2011)

how_it_works.simple: Own a little of the money of about 20 emerging countries, equally, against the US dollar, and collect their higher interest.
how_it_works.analogy: Like an index fund, but for the currencies of fast-growing countries.
how_it_works.precise: Equal-weighted long position in one-month forwards (or spot plus interest gap) on about 20 EM currencies against USD, rebalanced monthly and rolled with FX swaps. Gilmore and Hayashi report a Sharpe ratio of 1.34 over January 1999 to September 2008 and estimate rolling costs of about 30 basis points a year.

rule: Monthly: equal weight long every EM currency with a price and a rate, funded in USD; total gross exposure 1.
data_needed: Daily EM spot rates (ECB reference rates)
economic_rationale: EM currencies paid a large interest premium and, in the authors' sample, did not depreciate enough to offset it; diversification across regions kept volatility low.
why_it_might_fail: The sample (1999 to 2008) was an EM boom with a falling dollar and ends a month before the 2008 crash; the authors worked for or consulted for Banque AIG and used proprietary data.

reported_results.source: Gilmore and Hayashi (2008 NBER version), Table 3, EM20 long-only in USD
reported_results.notes: Mid rates. Same table: G9 majors 2.8% a year, volatility 7.3%, Sharpe 0.38. The authors estimate rolling costs of about 30 bp a year for EM, doubled in autumn 2008.

post_publication_evidence: None found by us. Everything after September 2008 is outside the authors' sample.

relevance.reason: Simple to rebuild with free data, and the whole post-2008 period is an untouched out-of-sample test of a well-known result.

research.notes: Added from RES-0013 and RES-0014 on 2026-10-21. Registered on 2026-10-21 as REG-0006 (em_fx_basket), not yet run.
